title: Add database migration system with Cloud Run Job
description:
Replace the current schema-in-container approach with a proper migration system using dbmate.

## Implementation Plan
See: `~/.claude/plans/soft-marinating-reddy.md`

## Why
- Current approach only handles initial schema creation (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS)
- Cannot handle schema changes like adding columns, indexes, or constraints
- As the app evolves, we need version-controlled, incremental migrations

## Decisions

### Tool: dbmate
Language-agnostic, pure SQL migrations, single Go binary
- Works regardless of backend language (Node, Java, Python, etc.)
- Migrations are pure .sql files — portable and easy to review
- Simple CLI: `dbmate up`, `dbmate new <name>`
- Lightweight container for Cloud Run Job

### 1. Migration directory: `db/migrations/`
Backend-agnostic, clear intent, common convention. Keeps infrastructure separate from application code.

### 2. Local development: docker-compose auto-migrate
Zero friction — developers cannot forget. Add a `db-migrate` service that runs before the backend starts. Falls back to manual `dbmate up` for non-Docker workflows.

### 3. Rollback strategy: Forward-only
Rollbacks with production data are risky and rarely tested. When something breaks, fix forward with a new migration. Simpler, safer, less code to maintain.

Safety net: Pre-migration backups + tested restore procedure (see habitcraft-af1).

### 4. Initial migration: Baseline
Existing prod DB gets marked as "at v1" (dbmate stores this in `schema_migrations` table). New environments run all migrations from scratch. Clear separation between "initial state" and "changes."

### 5. Schema dump: Enabled
Low cost (one auto-generated file), high value: see full schema at a glance during code review, bootstrap test databases quickly, documentation that stays in sync.

### 6. CI/CD sequencing: Sequential (migrate → deploy)
Simple and safe. Migrations are usually fast (seconds). If migration fails, deployment stops — which is exactly what you want. No complex retry logic needed.

## Scope

### Core Implementation (Done)
1. ✅ Add dbmate to the project (Docker image or binary)
2. ✅ Set up `db/migrations/` directory structure
3. ✅ Convert existing schema.sql to baseline migration
4. ✅ Configure dbmate for schema dump
5. ✅ Add db-migrate service to docker-compose for local dev
6. ✅ Create Cloud Run Job for running migrations in CI/CD
7. ✅ Update CI/CD to run migration job before deploying services
8. ✅ Document migration workflow for developers
9. ✅ Add pre-migration backup in CI/CD workflow

### CI Hardening (Done)
10. ✅ Unify seed data: use test-fixtures.sql for local and CI (folded from habitcraft-3fi)
11. ✅ Add dbmate status check before up in CI (fail fast)
12. ✅ Add post-migration verification step in CI

### Production Readiness (Done)
13. ✅ Rollback/recovery strategy documented and tested (habitcraft-af1)

## References
- dbmate: https://github.com/amacneil/dbmate
- Cloud Run Jobs docs: https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/create-jobs

title: Review and document rollback/recovery strategy for migrations
description:
Production readiness gate for the database migration system.

## Context
The migration system uses a forward-only strategy (no rollbacks). This decision has been reviewed and accepted, contingent on having robust backup/restore procedures that are tested and documented.

## Decisions Made

### Forward-Only with Strong Backup Safety Net
Forward-only is acceptable for HabitCraft because:
- Most migrations are low-risk schema changes
- Pre-migration backups are automated in CI/CD
- Point-in-time recovery is enabled in Cloud SQL
- We can fix forward quickly for most issues

The safety net is the backup/restore capability, which must be tested and documented.

### Temporary Instances for Testing (No Staging)
A full staging environment is not needed at this stage. Instead:
- Use temporary Cloud SQL clones to test restore procedures
- Clone from production backup, test, then delete
- Revisit staging decision as project grows

## Scope

### 1. Test Restore Procedure
Using temporary Cloud SQL instance:
```bash
# Clone prod for testing
gcloud sql instances clone habitcraft-prod-db habitcraft-restore-test

# Test restore from backup
gcloud sql backups restore BACKUP_ID --restore-instance=habitcraft-restore-test

# Verify data, measure timing
psql -h <IP> -U habitcraft -d habitcraft -c "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users;"

# Clean up
gcloud sql instances delete habitcraft-restore-test
```

Document:
- Exact steps performed
- Time taken for each step
- Any issues encountered

### 2. Document RTO/RPO
Based on actual tested restore times:
- **RTO (Recovery Time Objective)**: How long to restore service?
- **RPO (Recovery Point Objective)**: How much data could be lost?

### 3. Incident Runbook & Deployment Checklist
Combined document covering:

**Pre-deployment checklist:**
- [ ] Backup created (automated, but verify)
- [ ] Migration tested locally
- [ ] Migration reviewed

**Incident response ("migration broke prod"):**
1. How to identify the problem
2. Decision tree: fix forward vs restore
3. Exact commands to restore from backup
4. How to verify restoration worked
5. Post-incident communication

**Verification steps:**
- [ ] Services healthy after migration
- [ ] Key queries return expected results
- [ ] No error spikes in monitoring

## Deliverables
- [ ] Tested restore procedure with documented timing
- [ ] RTO/RPO added to db/README.md
- [ ] Incident runbook & deployment checklist in db/README.md
close_reason: Completed: tested restore (~15-22 min), documented RTO/RPO, added incident runbook and pre-deployment checklist

title: Add max password length validation
description:
No max length on password input. Long passwords cause CPU exhaustion with bcrypt hashing (DoS vector).

## Implementation Notes
1. Add max length validation (72 chars) to password in `backends/node/routes/auth.js`
   - Line ~60: Update `body('password').isLength({ min: 8 })` to `body('password').isLength({ min: 8, max: 72 })`
   - 72 is bcrypt's actual limit (truncates beyond that anyway)
2. Add same validation to password change in `backends/node/routes/users.js` (line ~184)
3. Add test cases for passwords exceeding 72 chars
4. Update any API docs/OpenAPI spec if applicable

## Files to modify
- backends/node/routes/auth.js (register, login validation)
- backends/node/routes/users.js (password change validation)
- backends/node/routes/auth.test.js
- backends/node/routes/users.test.js
close_reason: Implemented max 72 char password validation in frontend and backend

title: Harden migration system for production safety
description:
Add safety checks and verification to the migration system before production deployment.

## Tasks
1. **Add dbmate status check before up in CI** - Fail fast if migrations look wrong
2. **Add post-migration verification** - Query to confirm schema is correct after migration
3. **Update db/entrypoint.sh with dry-run option** - Allow status-only mode for verification
4. **Add pre-migration backup step** - Snapshot Cloud SQL before running migrations
5. **Create production deployment checklist** - Document one-time baseline setup and verification steps

## Why
- Migrations touching production data are high-risk
- Need visibility into what will run before it runs
- Need ability to recover if something goes wrong
- First production deployment requires manual baseline marking

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CI shows pending migrations before applying
- [ ] CI verifies schema after migration completes
- [ ] Cloud Run Job creates backup before running
- [ ] db/README.md has clear production deployment checklist
- [ ] Manual walkthrough completed successfully
